title: Shared PDF rendering foundation
description: LODGY-37 (per-invoice PDF acknowledgement) and LODGY-45 (full-data printable PDF export) both need to generate PDFs, and the app currently has zero PDF infrastructure - LODGY-23 deliberately shipped CSV-only and explicitly skipped PDF generation. Build one shared renderer that both consumers use, instead of two independent, inevitably-inconsistent PDF pipelines. This is a prerequisite for LODGY-37 and LODGY-45 - land this first. Implementation choice (native PdfDocument API vs. a PDF library) is no longer constrained by APK size - LODGY-48 was marked Won't Do, so pick whichever approach is simplest to get right (a library is fine if it saves real implementation risk, e.g. around Devanagari text shaping/pagination).
acceptanceCriteria: A single PDF-rendering module exists (page setup, text/table layout helpers, Devanagari-safe font handling for Hindi-language content per LODGY-30) that isn't tied to one specific document's content
Produces valid, correctly-paginated multi-page PDFs when content overflows a single page
LODGY-37 and LODGY-45 both consume this module rather than each rolling their own PDF generation

history.note: Added following backlog review: splitting LODGY-39, giving LODGY-37/45 a shared PDF prerequisite, and folding in the latest round of direct feedback (a real delete-without-confirmation bug hit on Rooms, a default-language reversal, and new notification/navigation-polish requests).

Starting - one PDF module both LODGY-37 and LODGY-45 will consume. Going with the platform PdfDocument rather than a library: Android already shapes and embeds Devanagari through its system typeface, so a library buys nothing here. Splitting the pure layout maths (wrapping, pagination, repeated table headers) out from the Canvas calls so the part that can actually get pagination wrong is JVM-testable.

Built the shared PDF module under com.lodgy.app.pdf, deliberately split so the risky part is testable. PdfContent.kt is the content model (Title/Heading/Paragraph/KeyValue/Table/Spacer + PdfDocumentContent) with no drawing concepts in it. PdfLayout.kt holds A4-at-72pt geometry plus two pure functions: wrapText(), which greedy-wraps against a caller-supplied measurer (so a word wider than the column lands on its own line instead of being dropped or looping), and paginate(), which splits measured lines into pages and re-emits a table's header row at the top of every page that table continues onto. PdfBlockLayout.kt turns blocks into wrapped, measured PdfLines through a TextMeasurer fun-interface - Paint on a device, a fixed-width stub in tests. LodgyPdfRenderer.kt is the only file that touches Canvas: it paginates, then draws each page with a running header, a rule, and an 'n / N' footer. Chose the platform android.graphics.pdf.PdfDocument over a PDF library on purpose - Android's system typeface already shapes Devanagari and PdfDocument embeds what it draws, so Hindi content per LODGY-30 renders correctly without shipping and subsetting a font, and LODGY-48 being Won't Do removed the only argument for the alternative. PdfLayoutTest covers wrapping (including the over-long word and empty input), single-page and multi-page splits, repeated table headers across a break, a line taller than a page not looping, empty content still yielding a page, and block-to-line conversion. LODGY-37 and LODGY-45 both build on this. testDebugUnitTest green.
